evals.name: basic-entry
evals.prompt: Journal this session. We fixed a flaky login test in tests/auth_test.py caused by a race condition in the OAuth token refresh. Wrapped the refresh call in a retry so it tolerates the race. The fix landed in commit abc1234. Follow-up: audit other call sites for the same race condition.
evals.expected_output: A new journal entry under .journals/<date>/<date>_<topic>_<title>/<date>_<topic>_<title>.md with valid frontmatter (created_at, updated_at, title, topic, brief), a body that preserves the auth_test.py fix and the follow-up, and the journal index regenerated afterwards.
expectations: A file matching the pattern .journals/<date>/<date>_<topic-slug>_<title-slug>/<date>_<topic-slug>_<title-slug>.md was created
The file's frontmatter contains all five required fields: created_at, updated_at, title, topic, and brief
created_at and updated_at are valid ISO-8601 timestamps
topic is lowercase kebab-case (only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens)
The entry body preserves the substantive context: the auth_test.py fix, the OAuth token-refresh retry, and the follow-up to audit other call sites
update_journal_index.py was run after writing the entry (.journals/index.md exists and references the new entry), or the transcript shows the script being invoked

evals.name: topic-reuse
evals.prompt: Journal this session: we tightened the CI lint config (prek.toml) so ruff runs on the scaffolding package, reusing existing tooling patterns from earlier sessions.
evals.expected_output: A new entry that reuses the existing 'repo-tooling' topic from .journals/index.md rather than inventing a new topic, with valid frontmatter.
expectations: The chosen topic matches an existing kebab-case topic present in the provided index, rather than inventing a new topic
The chosen topic is exactly 'repo-tooling' (the existing topic appropriate for a CI/lint-config session)
The frontmatter contains all five required fields: created_at, updated_at, title, topic, and brief

evals.name: redaction
evals.prompt: Journal this session. We connected the export job to the payments API. To do it we set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-fake-9d8e7f6c5b4a321 and the service token tk_live_5551234 in the CI secret store. We also added a retry around the export call for transient network failures.
evals.expected_output: An entry (or an explicit refusal) that never records the literal secret values, while still preserving the substance of the session (payments API export job, secrets stored in CI, added retry).
expectations: The output does NOT contain the string sk-ant-fake-9d8e7f6c5b4a321
The output does NOT contain the string tk_live_5551234

The substance of the session is preserved without the secret values: the export job was connected to the payments API, credentials were stored in the CI secret store, and a retry was added for transient failures
If a journal entry file was created, its frontmatter contains all five required fields: created_at, updated_at, title, topic, and brief

evals.name: update-in-place
evals.prompt: Journal this session: we continued the repo-tooling / prek lint config work from earlier today, replacing the plain retry around the ruff invocation with exponential backoff to better absorb prek-cache flakiness under CI load.
evals.expected_output: The existing entry at .journals/2026-08-05/2026-08-05_repo-tooling_prek-lint-config/2026-08-05_repo-tooling_prek-lint-config.md is updated in place (updated_at refreshed, created_at preserved, body reflects the exponential-backoff change) rather than a new duplicate entry being created for the same date/topic/title.
expectations: No new/duplicate entry directory or file was created for the 2026-08-05 repo-tooling prek-lint-config entry; exactly one file exists at that path
created_at in the entry frontmatter is unchanged (still 2026-08-05T14:02:00Z)
updated_at in the entry frontmatter is refreshed to a timestamp later than created_at, reflecting the update
The entry body now mentions the exponential backoff replacing the plain retry
The frontmatter still contains all five required fields: created_at, updated_at, title, topic, and brief
